topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, learning objectives, and historical framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling and proliferation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades drive sustained proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how malignancies in both hematopoietic and epithelial tissues halt terminal cell differentiation while maintaining proliferation.

topics.label: Evasion of programmed cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells resist apoptosis through alterations in p53 signaling and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress-response pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere dynamics, senescence bypass mechanisms, and p53 stress responses regulate cellular lifespan and summarize cell-autonomous growth control.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways such as aerobic glycolysis and the Krebs cycle to support growth and epigenetic regulation.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how growing tumors overcome diffusion limits by activating new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and biology of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step invasion-metastasis cascade, metastatic inefficiency, genomic features, and clinical monitoring of disseminating cancer cells.

topics.label: Conclusion and final remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides concluding reflections on the hallmarks of cancer and closes the lecture.
